name: Sika Boom-420 Fire
paste:
SIKA BOOM®-420 FIRE: SPECIFICATION CLAUSE SET

Source: Sika Boom®-420 Fire, March 2025, Version 02.02 (https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/q/sika_boom_-420_fire.pdf)
Draft for specifier review. Wording, values and standards are quoted from that data sheet; where it is silent the clause says 'Refer to manufacturer.' Confirm the current edition before issue.

1 SCOPE
1.1 Work included. Provide Sika Boom®-420 Fire where documented, installed or applied in accordance with this clause and the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (March 2025, Version 02.02).
1.2 Product description. Sika Boom®-420 Fire is a 1-part, fire resistant, self-expanding polyurethane foam. It meets the fire resistance requirements of up to 180 minutes according to AS 1530.4:2014. The combi-valve allows for precise, easy and effecient application by either gun or nozzle.
1.3 Intended uses stated by the manufacturer.
    - Restores the fire resistance performance of a floor or wall which incorporates linear seals
    - Interior use only
1.4 Limits of use. Observe the manufacturer's limitations stated in clause 4.7.

2 MATERIALS
2.1 Product. Sika Boom®-420 Fire
    - Product type as printed on the data sheet: FIRE RESISTANT POLYURETHANE EXPANDING FOAM
    - Supplier as printed on the data sheet: Sika Australia Pty Limited, ABN 12 001 342 329, aus.sika.com, Tel: 1300 22 33 48
2.2 Sustainability.
    - VOC emission classification GEV-Emicode EC1PLUS, license number 10376/03.06.13
2.3 Certificates and test reports.
    - AS1530.4:2014 fire resistance up to 180 minutes.
    - CE Marking and Declaration of Performance to ETA 24/0105, based on EAD 350140-00-1106:2017 – Fire stopping and fire sealing products, linear joint and gap seals
2.4 Standards and test methods cited in the data sheet. Cited as written in the data sheet. A citation is not a statement that the product complies with it; conformity is stated only where the data sheet says so (see the approvals clause and the statements quoted in the other clauses).
    - AS 1530.4:2014: cited elsewhere in the data sheet. Where: Description (p.1).
    - AS1530.4:2014: listed under approvals, certificates or standards. Where: Certificates And Test Reports (p.1).
    - ETA 24/0105: listed under approvals, certificates or standards. Where: Certificates And Test Reports (p.1).
    - EAD 350140-00-1106:2017: listed under approvals, certificates or standards. Where: Certificates And Test Reports (p.1).
    - DIN 4102-1: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Reaction to fire (p.2).
2.5 Characteristics stated by the manufacturer.
    - Fire resistance up to 180 minutes depending on the configuration
    - Combi-valve for gun or nozzle application
    - 1-Part ready to use
    - Safety valve for extended shelf life
    - Cured foam can be cut, trimmed and sanded
2.6 Composition, appearance and supply.
    - Composition: Polyurethane foam
    - Colour: Pink
2.7 Density.
    | Gun applied cured foam | 17±5 kg/m³ |
    | Nozzle applied cured foam | 30±5 kg/m³ |
2.8 Properties stated by the manufacturer.
    - Reaction to fire: B1 (DIN 4102-1)
    - Resistance to fire: Refer to ‘Approvals / Certificates’ section, Sika Passive Fire Stopping Solution Finder for linears seals or contact Sika Technical Services for specific information.
    - Light and thermal resistance: Not permanently UV-stable
    - Service temperature: −40 °C min. / +80 °C max. (briefly up to +100 °C)
    - Joint design: Refer to ‘Approvals / Certificates’ section, Sika Fire Stopping Solution Finder for Linear Seals or contact Sika Technical Services for specific information
2.9 Post expansion.
    | Gun applied | ~60 % |
    | Nozzle applied | ~160 % |
2.10 Packaging, shelf life and storage.
    - Packaging: 750 ml pressurised canister with safety valve: 12 canisters per box
    - Shelf life: 12 months from the date of production.
2.11 Storage conditions. The product must be stored in original, unopened and undamaged packaging in dry conditions at temperatures between +10 °C and +20 °C. Store in an upright position. Protect the canister from direct sunlight and temperatures above +50 °C (danger of exploding). Always refer to packaging.

3 SUBSTRATE PREPARATION
3.1 General. Prepare substrates in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (March 2025, Version 02.02) and the requirements below. Inspect the substrate against these requirements before application.
3.2 Substrate preparation.
    - The substrate must be clean, sound, firm, free from oils, grease, dust and loose or friable particles. Paint, cement laitance and other poorly adhering contaminants must be removed.
    - Pre-dampen the substrate with clean water, this ensures that Sika Boom®-420 Fire cures properly and also prevents secondary foam expansion.

4 APPLICATION
4.1 General. Apply in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (March 2025, Version 02.02) and the requirements below.
4.2 Application data.
    - Tack free time: 7±2 mins
4.3 Yield. 750 ml canister:
    | Box Yield | Gun applied | ~44 l |
    | Nozzle applied | ~30 l |
    | Joint Yield | Gun applied* | ~32 m |
    | Nozzle applied* | ~24 m |
    (Table as printed; a cell that wraps appears over several rows.)
    *Based on a 20 × 50 mm joint
    Test method printed: (FEICA TM 1003)
    Test method printed: (FEICA TM 1002)
4.4 Cutting time.
    | Gun applied: | ~25 minutes* |
    | Nozzle applied: | ~40 minutes* |
    *After this time a 30 mm diameter bead can be cut
4.5 Application. Shake Sika Boom®-420 Fire canister thoroughly (at least 20 times) prior to use, repeat shaking after long interuptions of use. Attach the canister to the application gun or attach nozzle to the canister combi-valve, apply the foam by holding the can and pointing the nozzle into the area of application then applying pressure to the nozzle trigger. The amount of foam applied can be regulated by the pressure applied to the nozzle. Ensure applications in deep voids are applied in layers allowing each layer to fully cure before application of the next layer. Applied foam must be allowed access to sufficient moisture in order to fully cure. Fully cured foam can be cut to shape.
4.6 Cleaning of equipment. Clean all tools and application equipment with Sika Boom® Cleaner or Sika® Remover-208 immediately after use. Clean the application gun by screwing Sika Boom® Cleaner onto the thread of the application gun and press the trigger to clean it. Do not leave the Sika Boom® Cleaner screwed on the application gun, as the valve could be damaged. Hardened material can only be mechanically removed.
4.7 Limitations and important considerations.
    - Limitations regarding dimensions and configurations described in the relevant fire resistance classification reports must be considered.
    - Moisture is necessary to cure the foam. Insufficient moisture may lead to subsequent unintended foam expansion (post-expansion).
    - Do not use for mechanical or structural fixing purposes.
    - Sika Boom®-420 Fire adheres without primers and/or activators to building materials in combination with which fire tests have been carried out.
    - Sika Boom®-420 Fire does not bond onto polyethylene (PE), polypropylene (PP), polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE / Teflon), and silicone, oil, grease or release agents.
    - The properties of the cured foam will be different between the gun and nozzle application.
    - Sika Boom®-420 Fire is not resistant to UV light.
4.8 Further documentation.
    - Safety Data Sheet

5 QUALITY CONTROL AND TESTING
5.1 Hold point. Before each application, measure and record the conditions in clause 5.2 and compare them with the manufacturer's limits. HOLD POINT: do not proceed until the Superintendent has released the hold point.
5.2 Material temperature.
    | Optimum | +20 °C |
    | Permissible | +5 °C min. / +30 °C max. |
5.3 Ambient air temperature.
    | Optimum | +20 °C |
    | Permissible | +5 °C min. / +30 °C max. |
5.4 Substrate temperature.
    | Optimum | +20 °C |
    | Permissible | +5 °C min. / +30 °C max. |
5.5 Conditions stated in the limitations. Also stated in the data sheet limitations (clause 4.7):
    - Moisture is necessary to cure the foam. Insufficient moisture may lead to subsequent unintended foam expansion (post-expansion).
5.6 Test methods printed beside stated values. Each value is as printed in the data sheet with its test method.
    - Reaction to fire: B1 (DIN 4102-1)
    - Yield: Box Yield | Gun applied | ~44 l; Nozzle applied | ~30 l; Joint Yield | Gun applied* | ~32 m; Nozzle applied* | ~24 m; 750 ml canister: *Based on a 20 × 50 mm joint (FEICA TM 1003) (FEICA TM 1002)
5.7 Basis of the stated values. All technical data stated in this Product Data Sheet are based on laboratory tests. Actual measured data may vary due to circumstances beyond our control.
5.8 Other tests. For any test method, sampling frequency or acceptance criterion not stated in this clause: refer to manufacturer and the project specification.

6 WARRANTY AND DOCUMENTATION
6.1 Documents to be obtained and submitted. Obtain the current issue of each document before ordering and submit it with the product submission. Documents are listed as published on the manufacturer's website.
    - Product Data Sheet: Sika Boom®-420 Fire, March 2025, Version 02.02, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/q/sika_boom_-420_fire.pdf
    - Safety Data Sheet: SDS Sika Boom®-420 Fire, version 18/06/2025, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/w/sds-sika-boom-420fire.pdf
6.2 Ecology, health and safety. For information and advice on the safe handling, storage and disposal of chemical products, users shall refer to the most recent Safety Data Sheet (SDS) containing physical, ecological, toxicological and other safety-related data.
6.3 Warranty. Obtain any product or installation warranty in writing from the manufacturer or its authorised applicator and file it with the project records. Warranty terms: refer to manufacturer.
    - Legal notes: In practice, the differences in materials, substrates and actual site conditions are such that no warranty in respect of merchantability or of fitness for a particular purpose, nor any liability arising out of any legal relationship whatsoever, can be inferred either from this information, or from any written recommendations, or from any other advice offered.
6.4 Local restrictions. Please note that as a result of specific local regulations the declared data for this product may vary from country to country. Please consult the local Product Data Sheet for the exact product data.
6.5 Application records. Record the product name, batch numbers, dates, areas treated and the conditions measured under clause 5.2, and include the records in the project documentation.
